title: verify() returns Ok even when all signers fail; caller must inspect signers vec
description: verify() returns Ok(VerificationResult) whenever the outer DER parses, even when every SignerInfo fails verification. The doc comment says 'The caller should check whether at least one signer has verified == true' but this is easy to miss. A caller who does 'verify(...)?' and then uses the result without checking result.signers[*].verified will accept a forged or invalid signature as valid. This is a security footgun in the public API. The pattern 'Ok means success' is the universal Rust expectation; deviating from it without a prominent warning generates real security bugs in downstream code.
